newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Chubb Security H1 hurt by S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Chubb Security H1 hurt by S.Africa.

text.p: Britain's Chubb Security Plc said on Tuesday its first-half results were hurt by market weakness in South Africa and continental Europe.
"We had some disappointment in South Africa and Europe," chief executive David Peacock told Reuters in an interview.
"We got our callibration wrong in South Africa. We expanded, but the market was slightly out of phase with that. The situation will improve in the second half there," he added.
The security services provider's first-half pretax profit of 46.1 million stg came at the low end of market expectations, which ranged from 46.5 to 48.0 million stg.
Chubb expected its acquisition of MSS Security and James Hardie Building Services to dilute earnings by about 3.0 million stg in 1996/97.
Peacock would not comment on analysts' forecasts.

"We're confident of our position. And the continued growth of the electronic security and fire protection businesses will benefit operating profit in the second half," he said, adding that Chubb's expansion in Asia would also boost results.
